title: The 1RB0LE two-word sweepers: one chain law for every era (Lean), and 510 eras followed with no halt
text: In 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA1LF_0LC0RA_0LB--- and its four 1RB0LE siblings, every layout right of the head is a chain of binary words, and each word that wraps sends 3 to the next. This chain law is proved in Lean for every number of words and every width (lean/Layers.lean, five copies), and it contains the cascade and the X layer. So within an era the right side is one counter, and an era changes only when a carry leaves the last word. A simulator that jumps over eras, running only the era changes cell by cell, followed 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA1LF_0LC0RA_0LB--- through 510 era changes (2.4·10<sup>297</sup> events) with no halt. C never runs out of digits; instead the chain keeps gaining words. What an era change hands on is still open.
